title: An older quiet day, shown as a mark
note: A "Not much today" saved by an older build holds a template sentence in the old row. The Book ignores that text and shows the same small "A quiet day" row; on a day that already has a letter no mark is listed. Counts say letters only. (Seeded fictional family Asha, with older-build rows.)

lines: Whatever you add this month lands here.
Bath time. You splash with your whole body, both hands, both feet, and then you check that I saw.
You rolled over all by yourself, twice, and then looked at me like you had always known how.
So it rained all morning so we sat by the window and you tried to catch the drops on the glass. You were so serious about it.
You smell like warm milk and the lavender soap Papa insists on. I could sit here all night.
You laughed today. A real one. It sounded like a little hiccup that surprised you as much as it surprised me.
Asha, you are four days old and the whole house is quiet. Your Nani made dal and nobody ate it because we were all watching you sleep.
